fine_trace.code: if (SMALL_XML < len) { xml = ALLOC_N(char, len); } else { xml = ALLOCA_N(char, len); }
fine_trace.note: When the XML string length is <= 4096 (SMALL_XML), the XML is copied into a stack-allocated buffer via ALLOCA_N, making pi->str point to a stack buffer.
The parser's current position pointer pi->s is initialized to the start of the stack-allocated XML buffer.
At the beginning of the children-reading loop, start is set to pi->s. If this is the first iteration and the element is at the very start of the XML, start == pi->str.
When start == pi->str, *(start - 1) reads 1 byte before the stack buffer. If that byte is whitespace or '>', the condition to decrement pi->s is satisfied.
pi->s is decremented to pi->str - 1, pointing before the start of the stack-allocated XML buffer.
read_text is called with pi->s pointing one byte before the stack buffer.
The first read in read_text reads *(pi->str - 1), which is 1 byte before the stack buffer - this is the dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1.

fine_trace.code: case '\0': set_error(&pi->err, "invalid format, document not terminated", pi->str, pi->s); return;
fine_trace.note: If the byte read before the buffer is '\0', set_error is invoked with xml=pi->str and current=pi->s (now equal to pi->str after the increment).

The loop dereferences *current. When current points at or before xml (the stack buffer start), the pointer comparison xml < current is false so the loop body is skipped, but the crash is attributed here because the out-of-bounds read of *(pi->str - 1) in read_text propagates through the error path into this function.
